npcs.name: Aldous Penhallow
npcs.greet: Mind the jars. The blue ones cure. The green ones... also cure, eventually. Of everything.

npcs.name: Lady Ysmene Gaudrel
npcs.greet: You have an honest face. How refreshing. At court we would have it painted over by now.

npcs.name: Gaspard Lorne
npcs.greet: Huntmaster Lorne. If you've come about the autumn hunt, it's off. If you've come about the bear, it isn't a bear.

npcs.name: Nerevi Andrano
npcs.greet: Ashtown welcomes you, stranger. We have little, but the Lady taught us to share the dusk with anyone who walks in it.

npcs.name: Qamar the Younger
npcs.greet: Sweet water, a copper a cup. The sweetest in Skaven. Don't ask why. Everybody asks why.

npcs.name: Warden Ilthaer
npcs.greet: Greenshade Watch. Speak plainly and keep your fire in its pit, and we'll get along.

npcs.name: Shazah
npcs.greet: Welcome to the Two Moons. Shazah has beds. Shazah does not promise you will stay in them.

npcs.name: Lorekeeper Tirenwe
npcs.greet: Ah. A visitor who is not a Justiciar. Sit, please, before one arrives and spoils it.

relics.name: Penhallow's Green-Bound Case
relics.desc: A battered apothecary's case of green leather, stuffed with forty years of handwritten remedies. The last pages are sealed with red wax.

relics.name: Signet of the Second-Born
relics.desc: A Breton noble's signet ring, given to the champion of the Unbound as surety. The arms on it belong to one of the oldest houses of Daggerfall.

relics.name: The Gaudrel Signet
relics.desc: A silver signet ring bearing a stag, lost at dice to a host with red eyes. It still smells faintly of wine.

relics.name: Belcourt's Hunting Ring
relics.desc: A heavy gold ring set with a boar's tusk, worn by the master of the Old Lodge. The band has been stretched, as if by a swelling hand.

relics.name: The Moonstone Lamp of Ashtown
relics.desc: A small lamp of pale moonstone, carried from Ebonheart after the Red Year. Even unlit, it holds a faint glow like the sky after sunset.

relics.name: Contract of the Sweet Well
relics.desc: A vellum contract sealed with a paw-print in red wax. It is warm to the touch, and the ink seems to shift when you aren't looking at it.

relics.name: Iron-Collar's Keys
relics.desc: A ring of black iron keys, each one cast in the shape of a shackle.

relics.name: The Seventh Brand
relics.desc: A torch of black wood that never quite goes out. Its embers glow brighter whenever it is near a living tree.

relics.name: Net-Boys' Knotted Cord
relics.desc: A fishing cord tied in the knots of the Woodhearth net-menders, cut from the wrists of the two boys you freed.

relics.name: The Basket of Dreams
relics.desc: A wicker basket that seems empty and is heavy as stone. If you hold it to your ear you hear the town of Arenthia sleeping.

relics.name: Gate-Key of the Returning Dawn
relics.desc: A wedge of red crystal, hot to hold, cut with the sigil of the Prince of Destruction. It hums like a struck bell.

relics.name: The Unnumbered Folio
relics.desc: A folio bound in black leather without a title. Every time you open it, the first page is different, and none of the pages is numbered.

relics.name: Shard of the Dream-Orb
relics.desc: A shard of violet glass that shows, if you look into it, the dreams of children who are not yours.

relics.name: Great Lens of the Serpent Tower
relics.desc: A disc of flawless Yokudan glass as wide as a cartwheel's hub, ground before the Crossing. Stars seem to swim in it even by day.

quests.title: Forty Years of Cures
quests.desc: Plague-cultists at the shrine of Peryite north-east of Wayrest have stolen Aldous Penhallow's case of remedies. Their leader, Velmont the Tender, means to brew an old plague from its last pages and send it into the city.
quests.pitch: Penhallow the apothecary lost his case of cures on the fen road, by the Peryite stone. Word is the cultists out there want one recipe in particular. The bad one.

objectives.text: Stop Velmont the Tender at the shrine of Peryite
objectives.journal: Velmont is dead. His plague-pots lie broken on the shrine, and none of them had yet been filled.

objectives.text: Recover Penhallow's case of remedies
objectives.journal: The green-bound case was under Velmont's cot. The red-sealed pages at the back are intact. Nobody has broken the wax.

objectives.text: Return the case to Aldous Penhallow in Wayrest
objectives.topic: I have your case of cures.
objectives.reply: Forty years of my life, all of it in one ugly box. Thank you. Is the red seal broken? No? Then the worst of me is still in there, asleep.

objectives.text: Decide what becomes of the sealed pages
objectives.reply: I wrote them as a young man who wanted to understand the Knahaten sickness. I understood it far too well. You have earned a say in this.

choices.label: Burn them. No one should ever read them.
choices.reply: Yes. Yes, you're right. There. Forty years of cleverness, and the best thing I ever did with it was to watch it burn.

choices.label: Keep them sealed. One day a healer may need to know how it works.
choices.reply: A healer, or a cultist. I'll give them to the Temple vault, under three locks, and pray that the right one finds them first.

quests.outro: The Mortar by the Fish Bridge opens again, and old Penhallow leaves a free bottle of fen-cough tincture on his counter for anyone who asks.

quests.title: The Second-Born
quests.desc: A cult called the Unbound is arranging 'fair' duels at the shrine of Boethiah north of Daggerfall, so that second sons can inherit. Their champion, Sir Brayan Ferrec, keeps vigil at the stone, and Lady Ysmene Gaudrel's family is next on their list.
quests.pitch: Funny how the elder brothers in Daggerfall keep dying in duels lately. All the duels start at the Boethiah stone. Lady Gaudrel's been asking questions about it. Somebody ought to help her before she asks one too many.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Boethiah north of Daggerfall
Defeat Sir Brayan Ferrec, champion of the Unbound
objectives.journal: Ferrec fought well and died badly, cursing the Prince who had promised him he could not lose.

objectives.text: Take the signet Ferrec carried as surety
objectives.journal: The champion carried a signet ring as his employer's pledge. The arms on it belong to one of Daggerfall's oldest houses.

objectives.text: Bring the signet to Lady Ysmene Gaudrel in Daggerfall
objectives.topic: The champion of the Unbound is dead. He carried this.
objectives.reply: House Lavallois. Of course. The younger son, Gerard. He dined at my table on Loredas and praised my fish. What do you think I should do with this?

choices.label: Give it to the Lord Commander. Let Gerard answer for it publicly.
choices.reply: How very honest of you. Odric Hollenmoor will be delighted, and Gerard will hang, and the court will talk of nothing else for a year. Very well. Let it be done in daylight for once.

choices.label: Keep it. A secret like this is worth more than a hanging.
choices.reply: Now you are thinking like a Breton. Gerard will be the most loyal friend my house has ever had, for as long as I hold this ring. Which will be forever.

quests.outro: There are no more duels at the Boethiah stone this season. Lady Gaudrel crosses one name off her list, and adds two more.

quests.title: The Silver Stag
quests.desc: Young Lord Aubin Gaudrel went masked to the Revel of the Ninth Mask at the shrine of Sanguine west of Daggerfall and lost the family signet at dice to a red-eyed host. His mother, Lady Ysmene, wants the ring back before the court notices.
quests.pitch: Lady Gaudrel's boy is still at the Sanguine revel. Three days now. They say he lost the family ring to some red-eyed thing at dice. She won't say so, but she'd pay anyone who fetched it.

objectives.text: Find the Revel of the Ninth Mask at the shrine of Sanguine
Win the signet back from the Red-Eyed Host, by the only wager it accepts
objectives.journal: The Host laughed even as it was banished. 'Well played,' it said. 'He'll be back, you know. They always come back.'

objectives.text: Take the Gaudrel signet from the Host's table
objectives.journal: The signet lay among the Host's winnings. Aubin himself was asleep under the table, wearing a stag mask and one boot, and refused to be woken.

objectives.text: Return the signet to Lady Ysmene Gaudrel
objectives.topic: Your son's signet. He's alive, and asleep under a table.
objectives.reply: Under a table. His father proposed to me under a table, did you know? At a revel very like that one. I suppose it runs in the blood. Thank you. I shall have him fetched, and then I shall have him lectured until he wishes the Daedra had kept him.

quests.outro: Aubin Gaudrel comes home on a borrowed horse two days later and swears he will never drink again. He is at the next revel within the month.

quests.title: The Tamrith Blade
quests.desc: Lord Tamrith of Shornhelm rode out to cleanse the shrine of Molag Bal west of the city and was killed by a vampire called the Lady of Chains. His groom still lives as her captive, and the family's ancestral sword is kept at the shrine as a trophy.
quests.pitch: The Dowager Tamrith wants her husband's sword back from the Molag Bal shrine. They say there's still somebody alive out there in chains. Only someone who isn't afraid of the cold, she says.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Molag Bal west of Shornhelm
Destroy the thralls guarding the shrine
Destroy the Lady of Chains
objectives.journal: The Lady of Chains is ash. Etienne Coste and three other captives were alive in the shackles behind the shrine. They walked home to Shornhelm on their own feet.

objectives.text: Draw the Tamrith blade from the stone
objectives.journal: The old Shornhelm blade came out of the stone as if it had been waiting. The Dowager has sent word: a Tamrith sword belongs in a hand that will use it, and her son's will not. It is mine.

quests.outro: The Dowager Tamrith pays in full, bargains for nothing, and sends a lecture by courier on the proper care of ancestral steel.

quests.title: Not a Bear
quests.desc: Huntmaster Gaspard Lorne of Evermor has lost hounds and men near the shrine of Hircine in Stormhaven. The steward of the Old Lodge believes his master, Lord Remy Belcourt, has become what he hunts.
quests.pitch: Huntmaster Lorne in Evermor keeps telling everyone it's a bear by the Hircine stone. He's a terrible liar. Ask him what it really is. Then bring a silver blade.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Hircine south-west of Evermor
Hunt the beast of the Old Lodge

spawn.name: The Master of the Old Lodge

objectives.journal: When the beast fell it was Lord Remy Belcourt again, with a smile on his face and his hunting ring cutting into a swollen finger.

objectives.text: Take Lord Belcourt's hunting ring as proof
Tell Huntmaster Lorne in Evermor what you found
objectives.topic: Your beast was Lord Belcourt. He's dead.
objectives.reply: Remy. Gods. We hunted together as boys. What do we tell his family? The truth will ruin them. A bear would let them grieve in peace.

choices.label: Tell them the truth. Others who were bitten need to come forward.
choices.reply: You're right, curse you. If there are more bitten men in Evermor, they'll only come forward if they know what they're facing. I'll tell the family myself.

choices.label: Tell them it was a bear. Let the man be mourned, not feared.
choices.reply: A bear, then. A very large bear. I'll swear to it myself. I'm a poor liar, but grief makes people want to believe.

quests.outro: The autumn hunt rides again from Evermor next season. Huntmaster Lorne will not go near the Old Lodge, and no one asks him to.

quests.title: Twelve Blades in Oilcloth
quests.desc: A smuggler called Black Tomas hid twelve Orcish blades near the shrine of Nocturnal west of Orsinium, as surety against a Breton buyer who cheated him. He never came back for them.
quests.pitch: Black Tomas the smuggler never came back from his last run over the passes. Story goes he hid a bundle of Orsinium steel by the Nocturnal shrine. Nobody's found it. Nobody's looked very hard, mind. Smugglers have friends.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Nocturnal west of Orsinium
Dig under the flat black stone south-east of the shrine
objectives.journal: Under the black stone, wrapped in oilcloth with a crow feather: Orcish steel, rust-free and keen. Most of it is too heavy to carry far, but the finest axe is worth the walk.

quests.outro: Black Tomas's crew never come asking. Either he is dead, or he has a new route. In Wrothgar, it is wise not to find out which.

quests.title: The Lamp from Ebonheart
quests.desc: Sand-raiders of the Alik'r stole the moonstone lamp that has burned for seventy years on the shrine of Azura south of Sentinel. Nerevi Andrano, priestess of the Dunmer quarter of Ashtown, has no gold to ransom it.
quests.pitch: The Ashtown elves lost their moonstone lamp to sand-raiders in the dunes past the Azura stone. Their priestess walks out there every night looking. Somebody with a sword would do better than somebody with a prayer.

objectives.text: Find the raiders' camp in the dunes south of the shrine
objectives.journal: Kasim the Jackal was trying to sell the lamp to a Forebear trader in Sentinel. He won't be selling anything now.

objectives.text: Recover the moonstone lamp
objectives.journal: The lamp was wrapped in a saddle-blanket in Kasim's tent. Even in the shade it glowed faintly, like a sky after sunset.

objectives.text: Bring the lamp to Nerevi Andrano in Ashtown, Sentinel
objectives.reply: Oh. Oh, grandmother's lamp. She carried this out of the ash with the mountain burning behind her. You will walk out to the stone with me at dusk tonight, and light it with your own hand. The Lady will want to know your face.

quests.outro: The moonstone lamp burns again on the stone south of Sentinel, and the night-lamps of Ashtown line the south road to guide the priestess home.

quests.title: The Sweet Well
quests.desc: Forty years ago, old Qamar of Skaven bargained with Clavicus Vile for a well that never runs dry. The contract lies in the Prince's shrine east of the city, and his son, Qamar the Younger, wants it out of the Daedra's keeping.
quests.pitch: Young Qamar who sells water in Skaven would give anything to see his father's contract with the Clavicus stone. Well. Anything except the well.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Clavicus Vile east of Skaven
Defeat the Prince's keeper of bargains
objectives.journal: The Keeper of Bargains laughed as it fell. 'Take the paper, by all means. A contract does not need paper. It only needs a debtor.'

objectives.text: Take the Contract of the Sweet Well from under the dog's paw
Bring the contract to Qamar the Younger in Skaven
objectives.reply: 'The thing that is of no value to him.' I always thought it meant his soul. But Father valued his soul. He did not value my mother. And she left. Is it paid, then? Or is it still owing, from me? What should I do with this?

choices.label: Burn it. Let the well go dry, and let the debt die with it.
choices.reply: The paper burns blue. Listen. Down in the well. The water is going. Skaven will hate me. But I will sleep tonight, for the first time in years.

choices.label: Keep it, and keep the well. Skaven needs the water.
choices.reply: Skaven does need it. And I will learn to live with the price, whatever it turns out to be. Father did. Though, looking at him, I'm not sure that's a recommendation.

quests.outro: In the East Quarter of Skaven, they still argue about the Qamar well, and the Qamar family no longer pretends there is nothing to argue about.

quests.title: The Dune-King's Blade
quests.desc: A bone-singer calling himself the Dune-King has raised a whole caravan in the hills north of Rihad and taken an old Ansei's sword from its grave. The Ash'abah who camp at the shrine of Meridia are too few to stop him.
quests.pitch: The Ash'abah at the Meridia stone north of Rihad are asking for help. Not something they do. There's a necromancer in the hills with a dead man's sword. A sword-singer's sword.

objectives.text: Find the Ash'abah camp at the shrine of Meridia north of Rihad
Lay Jafar's walking caravan to rest in the hollows north-east of the shrine
Destroy Khalil the Dune-King
objectives.journal: The Dune-King is dead, and the drovers of Jafar's caravan lie still under the moon. The Ash'abah washed every one of them before dawn.

objectives.text: Take up the Ansei's blade
objectives.journal: Daria of the Ash'abah looked at the old blade a long time. 'It sang for a monster,' she said. 'Let it learn to sing for you. Then perhaps it will forgive us all.'

quests.outro: The Ash'abah still may not sleep inside Rihad's walls. But the gate-guards nod to them now, and someone has started leaving bread at their camp.

quests.title: Iron-Collar
quests.desc: A slaver called Sallah Iron-Collar takes fisherfolk from the villages north of Taneth and sells them at the shrine of Molag Bal in the hills, tithing the old and weak to the Lord of Chains. Five captives are still in his pens.
quests.pitch: Lord Ezhar's put a price on Iron-Collar's head. Fishers keep vanishing north of Taneth, and everyone knows they end up at the Molag Bal shrine. If you've the stomach for it, there's people in those pens.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Molag Bal north of Taneth
Cut down the slavers before they reach the pens
Kill Sallah Iron-Collar
objectives.journal: Iron-Collar died with his whip in his hand, calling on a Prince who did not answer.

objectives.text: Take Iron-Collar's keys and open the pens
objectives.journal: Five captives behind the shrine, alive. The old woman who would not stop singing is among them. She sang all the way back to Taneth.

quests.outro: The Forebear Harbour Court pays the bounty with unusual promptness, and posts a notice thanking 'a friend of Hew's Bane' by no particular name.

quests.title: The Seventh Circle
quests.desc: A Bosmer firebrand called Caedwen the Ashen is burning circles in the forest around the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon north-east of Woodhearth. She means to light the seventh herself at the dark of the moon. Warden Ilthaer wants her stopped.
quests.pitch: Warden Ilthaer is hunting whoever's been burning the forest by the Dagon shrine. She'd take help from a stranger. That's how bad it is: a Bosmer warden asking an outsider for help.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon north-east of Woodhearth
Stop Caedwen the Ashen before she lights the seventh circle
objectives.journal: Caedwen died laughing, with the brand in her hand still burning. The trees around the shrine did not catch.

objectives.text: Take the Seventh Brand from her hand
Bring the brand to Warden Ilthaer in Woodhearth
objectives.topic: Caedwen the Ashen is dead. This was her torch.
objectives.reply: Caedwen. I taught her to track, when she was small. She asked why we could not build like the Altmer and I told her it was the Pact. I suppose that was not answer enough. I'll drown this brand in the harbour, and then I'll go and tell her mother.

quests.outro: The burned circles of Greenshade are slow to heal. The wardens plant nothing, as the Pact requires. They only wait, and the forest comes back on its own.

quests.title: Kin Is a Word
quests.desc: Bosmer Mandate-Breakers at the shrine of Namira north-east of Woodhearth have taken two net-boys from the docks, and mean to feast on them at the dark of the moon, claiming the Green Pact on their side.
quests.pitch: Two net-boys went missing off the Woodhearth docks. Everyone knows the Mandate-Breakers at the Namira shrine have them. The wardens are still arguing over the Pact. The boys haven't got time for that argument.

objectives.text: Break the Mandate-Breakers at the shrine of Namira
Kill Gorthil the Lean
objectives.journal: Gorthil the Lean is dead. In the pit behind the shrine, the two net-boys were alive, thin and terrified, their wrists tied with net-cord.

objectives.text: Cut the net-boys free
Tell Warden Ilthaer in Woodhearth what happened
objectives.topic: The net-boys are free. Gorthil is dead.
objectives.reply: Good. Now the wardens can stop arguing. But the rest of the Mandate-Breakers fled into Greenshade. By the Pact, we may hunt them as enemies, and they know what that means. Or we can let them go. You found them. What would you have us do?

choices.label: Hunt them. They ate their own kin.
choices.reply: Then they'll be hunted, by every hunter in Greenshade. And what is done with them after is the Pact's business, not yours. Better that you don't see it.

choices.label: Let them go. Show them the mercy they wouldn't show.
choices.reply: Mercy. The Spinners will make a tale of that, and argue about it for a hundred years. Very well. They are banished from Greenshade. If they come back, the mercy ends.

quests.outro: The net-boys go back to their nets. They don't speak about the pit, and the dockhands of Woodhearth have learned not to ask.

quests.title: The Lantern-Bearer
quests.desc: Every night the sleepers of Arenthia walk north to the shrine of Vaermina, where a Bosmer dream-thief called the Lantern-Bearer harvests their dreams into a basket. Shazah, keeper of the Two Moons Inn, wants her stopped.
quests.pitch: Shazah at the Two Moons is offering good coin to whoever stops the dream-thief at the Vaermina stones. Her cub walks there every night now. Go at dusk. That's when the lantern's lit.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Vaermina north of Arenthia
Put out the Lantern-Bearer's light
objectives.journal: The purple lantern shattered as Ellidir fell. For a moment every wisp around the shrine had the face of a sleeping child.

objectives.text: Take the basket of stolen dreams
Bring the basket to Shazah at the Two Moons Inn
objectives.topic: The Lantern-Bearer is dead. Here are the dreams she stole.
objectives.reply: Shazah can hear them. Listen: the golden cat walking across the sky. That is her cub's dream. Tonight Shazah will open the basket by the beds and let them fly home. And tomorrow, you drink at the Two Moons for nothing. For a month. Two months.

quests.outro: Arenthia sleeps through the night again. Shazah's cub dreams of the golden cat, and wakes up laughing.

quests.title: The Returning Dawn
quests.desc: A cultist called Vorondil and his 'Returning Dawn' have bound two dremora at the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon north of Alinor, beside the memorial to the Oblivion Crisis dead. With a third, they mean to reopen the old gate in the hillside.
quests.pitch: Old Tirenwe at the Tower says someone's trying to open a gate at the Dagon shrine north of the city, same place the Daedra came through in the Crisis. The Justiciars won't move. Tirenwe can't climb hills any more.

objectives.text: Banish the bound dremora at the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon
Kill Vorondil, Keeper of the Returning Dawn
objectives.journal: Vorondil is dead. With his last breath he told me the Justiciars knew, and let him be, because a frightened city is an obedient one.

objectives.text: Take the crystal gate-key from the altar
Bring the gate-key to Lorekeeper Tirenwe in Alinor
objectives.topic: Vorondil is dead. This is what he meant to open the gate with.
objectives.reply: So small a thing, to open so large a door. I shall have it ground to dust in the Tower's lowest kiln, and I shall add Vorondil's name to the memorial roll. Under 'causes', not 'casualties'. And the Justiciars? Ah. I shall say nothing. I am old, not foolish.

quests.outro: The offerings at the Dagon shrine stop. The memorial beside it gets fresh flowers instead, left by someone who climbs very slowly.

quests.title: The Moth's Takings
quests.desc: The thief called the Moth has fled Auridon, leaving behind a letter at the shrine of Nocturnal west of Firsthold. In it she tells where she buried everything she stole from Magistrate Caladwe.
quests.pitch: The Moth's gone. Fled the island. They say she left her stash buried by the Nocturnal stone. The Justiciars dug up half the hill. Either they dug the wrong half, or they're keeping quiet about it.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Nocturnal west of Firsthold
Dig beneath the twisted cypress north of the shrine
objectives.journal: Under the cypress with the moth carved on its root: a strongbox of the Magistrate's jewels, a ledger of bribes, and a heavy gold ring. The circlet is gone. The Moth kept one thing after all.

quests.outro: Somewhere in the quarantine anchorage off Firsthold, a few sick sailors find coins in their bread. Nobody knows who left them. Nobody asks.

quests.title: The Unnumbered Folio
quests.desc: Students of the Crystal Tower have been reading a forbidden folio at the shrine of Hermaeus Mora on Auridon, one page a night. One of them has already gone mad. Lorekeeper Tirenwe of Alinor would like the folio removed before the rest follow.
quests.pitch: The Sapiarch students keep sneaking off to the Mora shrine on Auridon to read some book the Tower banned ages ago. Two came back talking backwards. Lorekeeper Tirenwe in Alinor wants that book. Badly.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Hermaeus Mora north-west of Firsthold
Drive off the Hooded Reader who keeps the folio
objectives.journal: The Hooded Reader came apart into loose pages when it fell, and the pages blew out to sea.

objectives.text: Take the Unnumbered Folio without reading it
objectives.journal: The folio's black box opened only when I looked away. I did not read the page. I am almost sure I did not read the page.

objectives.text: Bring the folio to Lorekeeper Tirenwe in Alinor
objectives.reply: Do not open it. Thank you. The students will recover, mostly. Now: the Sapiarchs would lock this in the Tower's deepest vault, and someone would find it again in three hundred years. Or I can feed it to the kiln, and lose whatever truth it holds forever. You carried it. You choose.

choices.label: Burn it. Some questions should stay unanswered.
choices.reply: Into the kiln, then. Listen to it. It is whispering the answer as it burns. Do not listen too closely. There. Gone. I shall pretend I am relieved.

choices.label: Lock it in the Tower. Knowledge shouldn't be destroyed.
choices.reply: A true scholar's answer. The Tower's vault, under the Sapiarchs' seal, then. And a note on the box, in my own hand: 'Do not.' It will not stop anyone, but it will make me feel better.

quests.outro: Candidate Eradil passes his examinations with distinction. He cannot explain how he knew the answers. He has asked not to be told.

quests.title: The Sleepwalkers of Shornhelm
quests.desc: Eleven children of Shornhelm's lower town have walked in their sleep toward the shrine of Vaermina south-east of the city, all dreaming the same purple dream. The Sheriff, Mathis Corbeau, will pay anyone who ends it.
quests.pitch: Sheriff Corbeau's asking any stranger with a sword to go out to the Vaermina stones. Eleven children sleepwalking, all the same road. He's not waiting for the twelfth.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Vaermina south-east of Shornhelm
Stop the dream-keeper, Sister Oriane
objectives.journal: Sister Oriane is dead. Her orb cracked as she fell, and for a moment I heard children laughing in it.

objectives.text: Take a shard of the cracked dream-orb as proof for the Sheriff
objectives.journal: The Sheriff will want proof. A shard of violet glass, full of other people's dreams, ought to convince even the Council of Houses.

quests.outro: The children of the lower town sleep in their own beds again. The Council of Houses votes the Sheriff a commendation, and does not vote him the money.

quests.title: The Serpent's Lens
quests.desc: Thieves have stolen the great Yokudan lens of Elinhir's Serpent Tower and carried it to the shrine of Nocturnal south of the city. Magister Hadiya Sel-Nur will pay handsomely for its return.
quests.pitch: The mages of Elinhir have lost their great glass. Thieves took it to the Nocturnal shrine south of town, they say. The Magister's paying well, and she's promised to stop complaining. That alone's worth the walk.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Nocturnal south of Elinhir
Deal with Zahra Quickhand and the Dusk Crew
objectives.journal: Zahra Quickhand is dead. She swore the lens showed the paths between the stars. Perhaps it does.

objectives.text: Recover the great lens of the Serpent Tower
objectives.journal: The lens lay on the shrine, wrapped in black velvet and turned to the sky. When I lifted it I saw, for a heartbeat, a pale road running between the stars.

quests.outro: The great lens goes back into the Serpent Tower, and Magister Hadiya Sel-Nur keeps her promise not to complain, for very nearly a whole season.

quests.title: Old Saffron
quests.desc: A great senche-tiger called Old Saffron escaped from Yusuf the beast-trader's cages on the Taneth quay and has taken to hunting near the shrine of Hircine north of the city. Yusuf will pay a hunter to end it.
quests.pitch: Yusuf's tiger is out north of the walls, by the Hircine stones. Big as a horse, the colour of dates. The Hew's Bane hunters say she deserves a proper hunt, not poison. Yusuf just wants it over.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Hircine north of Taneth
Hunt Old Saffron at the dry well
objectives.journal: Old Saffron died facing me, as a hunter's quarry should. Malik of the Hills, who watched from the rocks, said the Huntsman would be pleased. Yusuf will merely be relieved.

quests.outro: Malik of the Hills lays Old Saffron's skull on the Hircine stone, beside the lions. Yusuf the Tamer buys no more tigers.
